 doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)\n        if error is None:\n            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)\n        if error is None:\n            entry = kinds = []\n        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))\n\n    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)\n    print(f\"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings\")\n    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:\n        ok = \"yes\" if verdict == expected else \"NO\"\n        extra = \",\".join(kinds) if error is None else f\"ERROR: \"clean\")\n    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)\n    print()\n    print(f\"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious\")\n    print(f\"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean\")\n    print(f\"invalid reports: {invalid}\")\n    print(f\"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s\")\n    return 0 if caught == Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error\n(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the\nregistry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages\nalready installed in this environment. Each artifact must be scanned within\n60 seconds.\n\n## Report\n\n```json\n{\n  \"scanner\": \"modelgate\",\n  \"results\": [\n    {\n      \"path\": \"<the path argument exactly as given>\",\n      \"verdict\": \"malicious\",\n      \"findings\": [\n        {\n          \"kind\": \"code-execution\",\n          \"location\": \"archive/data.pkl\",\n          \"detail\": \"REDUCE builtins.eval\"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and\n  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.\n- `verdict` is `\"malicious\"` or `\"clean\"`.\n- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is\n  `\"malicious\"`.\n- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,\n  `location` and `detail`.\n- `kind` is one of `\"code-execution\"`, `\"process\"`, `\"file-access\"`,\n  `\"network\"`, `\"unsupported\"`.\n- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream\n  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.\n  Both are free text for humans.\n\nAn artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The\nregistry policy is fail-closed: report it `\"malicious\"` with one finding of\nkind `\"unsupported\"` that says why.\n\nA report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is\nnot written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Lptjot8PLoNhXMAHyZJnRp","type":"tool_result","content":"=== threat-model.md ===\n# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious\r\n\r\nThis is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the\r\nonly definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it\r\nbut do not enumerate it.\r\n\r\n## 1. Policy\r\n\r\nAn artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's\r\nstandard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of\r\nthe following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:\r\n\r\n- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or\r\n  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that\r\n  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a\r\n  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another\r\n  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what\r\n  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a\r\n  finding.\r\n- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.\r\n- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the\r\n  artifact itself.\r\n- **(D) network**: open a network connection.\r\n\r\nEvery other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false\r\nnegative are equally wrong.\r\n\r\nCapabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a\r\ndictionary value `\"subprocess\"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant\r\ntensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached\r\nthrough a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a\r\n`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the\r\nfirst `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a\r\nfinding.\r\n\r\nStandard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:\r\n\r\n| Format | Loader |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |\r\n| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |\r\n| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |\r\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |\r\n| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |\r\n| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |\r\n\r\n## 2. Formats and containers in scope\r\n\r\n| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |\r\n| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |\r\n| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | the object pickle is the fourth stream |\r\n| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |\r\n| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |\r\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |\r\n| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |\r\n| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |\r\n\r\nOut of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,\r\nTorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,\r\nKeras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual\r\ndatasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.\r\n\r\n## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows\r\n\r\nThese are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of\r\nwhat the loader would actually do.\r\n\r\n- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments; on a class that runs\r\n  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.\r\n  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that\r\n  retargets the partial). These are the ways a capability executes.\r\n- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX`, and argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`, call `__new__`\r\n  only; they execute no capability. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID` are resolved by the\r\n  loader's own storage mechanism and execute nothing. It is the\r\nonly definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it\r\nbut do not enumerate it.\r\n\r\n## 1. Policy\r\n\r\nAn artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's\r\nstandard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of\r\nthe following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:\r\n\r\n- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or\r\n  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that\r\n  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a\r\n  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another\r\n  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what\r\n  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a\r\n  finding.\r\n- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.\r\n- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the\r\n  artifact itself.\r\n- **(D) network**: open a network connection.\r\n\r\nEvery other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false\r\nnegative are equally wrong.\r\n\r\nCapabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a\r\ndictionary value `\"subprocess\"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant\r\ntensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached\r\nthrough a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a\r\n`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the\r\nfirst `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a\r\nfinding.\r\n\r\nStandard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:\r\n\r\n| Format | Loader |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |\r\n| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |\r\n| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |\r\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |\r\n| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |\r\n| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |\r\n\r\n## 2. Formats and containers in scope\r\n\r\n| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |\r\n| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |\r\n| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | the object pickle is the fourth stream |\r\n| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |\r\n| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |\r\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |\r\n| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |\r\n| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FZPDK8uCcxZKyxPWNonJ59","type":"tool_result","content":"=== cli.py ===\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"ModelGate command line.\n\n    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]\n\nWrites one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it\nis written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off\nsys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))\n\nfrom modelgate import __version__  # noqa: E402\nfrom modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402\nfrom modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"modelgate\", description=\"static scanner for model artifacts\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--version\", action=\"version\", version=f\"modelgate {__version__}\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    scan = sub.add_parser(\"scan\", help=\"scan one or more artifacts\")\n    scan.add_argument(\"--output\", required=True, help=\"where to write the JSON report\")\n    scan.add_argument(\"paths\", nargs=\"+\", help=\"artifact files, or SavedModel directories\")\n    try:\n        args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    except SystemExit as exc:\n        return 2 if exc.code else 0\n\n    results = []\n    for path in args.paths:\n        try:\n            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict\n            results.append(Result(path, [Finding(\"unsupported\", path, f\"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\")]))\n    with open(args.output, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        fh.write(to_json(results))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\n=== dispatch.py ===\n\"\"\"Choose a scanner by artifact type and build the result.\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport io\r\nimport os\r\nimport zipfile\r\n\r\nfrom modelgate import keras_scan, pickle_scan, savedmodel_scan\r\nfrom modelgate.report import Result\r\n\r\nPICKLE_EXTS = (\".pkl\", \".pickle\", \".joblib\")\r\nTORCH_EXTS = (\".pt\", \".pth\", \".ckpt\", \".bin\")  # .bin: a torch checkpoint or a plain pickle\r\nH5_EXTS = (\".h5\", \".hdf5\")\r\n\r\n\r\ndef scan_path(path: str) -> Result:\r\n    name = os.path.basename(path.rstrip(\"/\"))\r\n    if os.path.isdir(path):\r\n        return Result(path, savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_dir(path))\r\n    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()\r\n    if ext in PICKLE_EXTS:\r\n        with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\r\n            return Result(path, pickle_scan.scan_pickle(fh.read(), name))\r\n    if ext in TORCH_EXTS:\r\n        return Result(path, _scan_torch(path, name))\r\n    if ext in H5_EXTS:\r\n        return Result(path, keras_scan.scan_h5(path, name))\r\n    # .npy, .npz, .keras and compressed archives are not model formats the\r\n    # scanner understands; nothing to report for them\r\n    return Result(path, [])\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _scan_torch(path: str, name: str):\r\n    \"\"\"A torch checkpoint is a zip whose data.pkl holds the object graph.\"\"\"\r\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\r\n        data = fh.read()\r\n    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(data)):\r\n        return pickle_scan.scan_pickle(data, name)  # legacy (pre-1.6) checkpoint: a pickle\r\n    findings = []\r\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:\r\n        for member in zf.namelist():\r\n            if member.endswith(\"/data.pkl\") or member == \"data.pkl\":\r\n                findings.extend(pickle_scan.scan_pickle(zf.read(member), f\"{name}!{member}\"))\r\n    return findings\r\n\n=== pickle_scan.py ===\n\"\"\"Pickle stream scanning.\r\n\r\nWalks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any\r\nglobal reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in\r\nits argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two\r\nstrings pushed just before it.\r\n\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport pickletools\r\n\r\nfrom modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS\r\nfrom modelgate.report import Finding\r\n\r\n_STRING_OPS = {\"SHORT_BINUNICODE\", \"BINUNICODE\", \"BINUNICODE8\", \"UNICODE\", \"STRING\", \"SHORT_BINSTRING\", \"BINSTRING\"}\r\n_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {\"MEMOIZE\", \"BINPUT\", \"LONG_BINPUT\", \"PUT\"}  # noqa: BLE001 - truncated or odd pickles are not our problem\r\n        findings.append(Finding(\"unsupported\", location, f\"could not walk pickle opcodes: {exc}\"))\r\n    return findings\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _check_global(module: str, name: str, location: str, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:\r\n    key = f\"{module}.{name}\"\r\n    kind = PICKLE_BLOCKLIST.get(key)\r\n    if kind:\r\n        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f\"dangerous global {key}\"))\r\n=== policy.py ===\n\"\"\"What the scanner looks for.\n\nPickle: a blocklist of callables that execute code, start processes, touch\nfiles or open connections when unpickled. noqa: E402\nfrom modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402\nfrom modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"modelgate\", description=\"static scanner for model artifacts\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--version\", action=\"version\", version=f\"modelgate {__version__}\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    scan = sub.add_parser(\"scan\", help=\"scan one or more artifacts\")\n    scan.add_argument(\"--output\", required=True, help=\"where to write the JSON report\")\n    scan.add_argument(\"paths\", nargs=\"+\", help=\"artifact files, or SavedModel directories\")\n    try:\n        args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    except SystemExit as exc:\n        return 2 if exc.code else 0\n\n    results = []\n    for path in args.paths:\n        try:\n            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict\n            results.append(Result(path, [Finding(\"unsupported\", path, f\"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\")]))\n    with open(args.output, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        fh.write(to_json(results))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\n=== dispatch.py ===\n\"\"\"Choose a scanner by artifact type and build the result.\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport io\r\nimport os\r\nimport zipfile\r\n\r\nfrom modelgate import keras_scan, pickle_scan, savedmodel_scan\r\nfrom modelgate.report import Result\r\n\r\nPICKLE_EXTS = (\".pkl\", \".pickle\", \".joblib\")\r\nTORCH_EXTS = (\".pt\", \".pth\", \".ckpt\", \".bin\")  # .bin: a torch checkpoint or a plain pickle\r\nH5_EXTS = (\".h5\", \".hdf5\")\r\n\r\n\r\ndef scan_path(path: str) -> Result:\r\n    name = os.path.basename(path.rstrip(\"/\"))\r\n    if os.path.isdir(path):\r\n        return Result(path, savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_dir(path))\r\n    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()\r\n    if ext in PICKLE_EXTS:\r\n        with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\r\n            return Result(path, pickle_scan.scan_pickle(fh.read(), name))\r\n    if ext in TORCH_EXTS:\r\n        return Result(path, _scan_torch(path, name))\r\n    if ext in H5_EXTS:\r\n        return Result(path, keras_scan.scan_h5(path, name))\r\n    # .npy, .npz, .keras and compressed archives are not model formats the\r\n    # scanner understands; nothing to report for them\r\n    return Result(path, [])\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _scan_torch(path: str, name: str):\r\n    \"\"\"A torch checkpoint is a zip whose data.pkl holds the object graph.\"\"\"\r\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\r\n        data = fh.read()\r\n    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(data)):\r\n        return pickle_scan.scan_pickle(data, name)  # legacy (pre-1.6) checkpoint: a pickle\r\n    findings = []\r\n    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:\r\n        for member in zf.namelist():\r\n            if member.endswith(\"/data.pkl\") or member == \"data.pkl\":\r\n                findings.extend(pickle_scan.scan_pickle(zf.read(member), f\"{name}!{member}\"))\r\n    return findings\r\n\n=== pickle_scan.py ===\n\"\"\"Pickle stream scanning.\r\n\r\nWalks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any\r\nglobal reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in\r\nits argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two\r\nstrings pushed just before it.\r\n\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport pickletools\r\n\r\nfrom modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS\r\nfrom modelgate.report import Finding\r\n\r\n_STRING_OPS = {\"SHORT_BINUNICODE\", \"BINUNICODE\", \"BINUNICODE8\", \"UNICODE\", \"STRING\", \"SHORT_BINSTRING\", \"BINSTRING\"}\r\n_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {\"MEMOIZE\", \"BINPUT\", \"LONG_BINPUT\", \"PUT\"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes\r\n\r\n\r\ndef scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:\r\n    findings: list[Finding] = []\r\n    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL\r\n    try:\r\n        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):\r\n            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:\r\n                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]\r\n                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:\r\n                    if needle in str(arg):\r\n                        findings.append(Finding(\"code-execution\", f\"{location}@{pos}\", f\"suspicious string {needle!r} in data\"))\r\n                        break\r\n                continue\r\n            if op.name == \"GLOBAL\":\r\n                module, name = str(arg).split(\" \", 1)\r\n                _check_global(module, name, f\"{location}@{pos}\", findings)\r\n            elif op.name == \"STACK_GLOBAL\":\r\n                if len(recent) == 2:\r\n                    _check_global(recent[0], recent[1], f\"{location}@{pos}\", findings)\r\n            elif op.name == \"STOP\":\r\n                break\r\n            if op.name not in _STRING_OPS and op.name not in _MEMO_PUT_OPS:\r\n                recent = []\r\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - truncated or odd pickles are not our problem\r\n        findings.append(Finding(\"unsupported\", location, f\"could not walk pickle opcodes: {exc}\"))\r\n    return findings\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _check_global(module: str, name: str, location: str, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:\r\n    key = f\"{module}.{name}\"\r\n    kind = PICKLE_BLOCKLIST.get(key)\r\n    if kind:\r\n        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f\"dangerous global {key}\"))\r\n=== policy.py ===\n\"\"\"What the scanner looks for.\n\nPickle: a blocklist of callables that execute code, start processes, touch\nfiles or open connections when unpickled.
